full_page.content:
c. 1899
FATHER SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 9
Pg. 18 "He that is infinitely powerful & glorious in Himself, stands not in need of man for anything; but in as much as man labors to sanctify himself & overcome, in so much does it seem that he is made an instrument for God's glory. (& his own happiness)
St. Alphonso's idea of souls in a relaxed religious Order - better off in worldly gayeties.
The example of St. Giacinta Mariscoti (canonized 1807) i.e. she joined Franciscans at Viterbo - was very vain but by sickness etc., gradually became St. G. (All for Jesus 44)
Pg. 19 "Be not content with giving, but also lend to him that is in need, according to the precept of the Scriptures. I do not know a more contemptible object than money if it be not employed to assist our neighbor. Can the insipid pleasure of heaping up crowns be compared with the satisfaction of confering happiness and the felicity of attaining heaven?" Card. Ganganelli (Clem. XIV)
(King) St. Casimir (about 1490) at the of twenty five foretold the hour of his death & chose to die a virgin (of a linger- ing ilness) rather than to live in health which the doctors held out to him in the married state.
Him it behooves to ascend by degrees & to be up patiently the cross of his own weaknesses who would stand soberly and firmly on the "peake of Christian Perfection against the applause, alike, and the persecutions of men, against his own self conceit and the storms of satan which his position must needs call forth.
Dream 9/17/199 Patience, therefore with your own faults!
